journal_name: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing

abstracts.abstract: This paper introduces a novel physics-informed graph neural network (Physics-GNN) framework that fundamentally transforms hyperspectral imaging analysis by unifying physical radiative transfer models with deep learning architectures. Unlike conventional data-driven approaches that treat spectral signatures as mere statistical patterns, the proposed framework embeds domain-specific physical constraints directly into the neural network architecture, enabling the model to respect conservation laws and atmospheric correction principles. We formalize the theoretical foundations of this integration, proving that the resulting architecture exhibits superior generalization properties when trained on limited labeled data. The framework introduces spectral message passing mechanisms that propagate physical relationships across neighboring pixels while maintaining interpretability. Extensive experiments on multiple hyperspectral datasets demonstrate that Physics-GNN achieves 15.3% higher classification accuracy compared to state-of-the-art methods while requiring 60% less training data. More importantly, the physical embeddings provide physically meaningful explanations for network predictions, addressing the long-standing interpretability challenge in remote sensing image processing. This work establishes a new paradigm for incorporating domain knowledge into deep learning for geoscience applications.

This paper presents a significant theoretical advancement in synthetic aperture radar (SAR) target recognition by developing a novel multi-scale attention mechanism that substantially improves feature extraction from polarimetric SAR imagery. Existing deep learning approaches suffer from limited capability in capturing hierarchical spatial patterns inherent in SAR data, resulting in suboptimal classification performance for complex land cover scenarios. The proposed attention framework introduces scale-aware feature fusion through novel cross-level attention modules that dynamically weight multi-resolution representations based on target characteristics. We theoretically analyze the convergence properties of the proposed attention mechanism and prove its effectiveness in reducing feature redundancy while preserving discriminative information. The framework incorporates polarimetric scattering characteristics into the attention computation, enabling more physics-consistent feature representations. Experimental validation on four benchmark SAR datasets reveals average classification accuracy improvements of 8.7% over previous state-of-the-art methods. The proposed mechanism demonstrates particular effectiveness for fine-grained land cover classification, achieving 12.4% improvement for complex urban categories. This work provides both theoretical insight and practical advancement for radar remote sensing applications.

This paper presents an innovative real-time multimodal Earth observation system that fundamentally reimagines the integration of LiDAR, hyperspectral, and SAR sensors for comprehensive environmental monitoring. The proposed system architecture introduces a novel sensor fusion framework that operates at the decision level, enabling synergistic utilization of complementary information from active and passive sensing modalities. The system implements a novel asynchronous processing pipeline that handles the inherent temporal misalignment between satellite acquisitions while maintaining sub-meter spatial registration accuracy. Key innovations include a lightweight edge computing module that enables onboard processing of 4K resolution imagery with 150ms latency, and an adaptive quality assessment module that automatically evaluates fusion performance in real-time. The complete system was deployed on a custom-built Earth observation platform and validated through extensive field campaigns covering diverse terrain including forests, agricultural lands, and urban areas. Quantitative evaluation demonstrates that the system achieves 94.2% classification accuracy for land cover mapping while reducing data transmission bandwidth by 78% compared to traditional approaches. This work establishes a new paradigm for operational Earth observation systems that bring geospatial analysis capabilities directly to the sensing platform.

This paper presents a substantially improved change detection system for satellite imagery that addresses critical challenges in operational environmental monitoring and disaster assessment. The proposed system advances the state-of-the-art through three key architectural innovations: a novel Siamese network backbone with enhanced feature extraction capabilities, an attention-based difference analysis module that effectively suppresses seasonal variations while highlighting genuine land cover changes, and a lightweight post-processing pipeline optimized for deployment on cloud computing platforms. The system introduces a new temporal consistency enforcement mechanism that significantly reduces false alarms in periodic monitoring scenarios, a persistent problem in existing operational systems. Implementation details are provided for a distributed processing architecture that handles daily ingestion of multi-temporal Sentinel-2 imagery across continental-scale regions. Comprehensive evaluation using historical disaster events demonstrates that the improved system achieves 89.6% detection accuracy with 67% reduction in processing time compared to previous approaches. The system has been successfully deployed for operational climate data analysis, processing over 15,000 image pairs monthly for monitoring deforestation and urban expansion. Results demonstrate robust performance across diverse geographic regions and climatic conditions.
